title: Burnout check
intro: Six questions about personal burnout from the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory. Your answers are not stored and are never shared with your employer.

instrument.name: Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI) – personal burnout scale
instrument.licence: Kristensen, T. S., Borritz, M., Villadsen, E., & Christensen, K. B. (2005). The Copenhagen Burnout Inventory. Free to use with attribution.

questions.text: How often do you feel tired?
How often are you physically exhausted?
How often are you emotionally exhausted?
How often do you think: "I can't take it anymore"?
How often do you feel worn out?
How often do you feel weak and susceptible to illness?

bands.title: Low burnout level
bands.body: Your responses suggest a low level of personal burnout. Keeping healthy routines can help you stay balanced.
bands.nextStep: Explore our wellbeing articles and tools for ideas on sustaining your energy.

bands.title: Moderate burnout level
bands.body: Your responses suggest a moderate level of personal burnout. It may help to talk to someone about what you are experiencing.
bands.nextStep: Consider speaking with a wellbeing professional through your employer's programme. All sessions are confidential.

bands.title: High burnout level
bands.body: Your responses suggest a high level of personal burnout. Professional support can make a real difference.
bands.nextStep: We recommend booking a confidential session with a psychologist through your employer's programme. Your employer never learns who used NestSelf or what was discussed.

bands.title: Severe burnout level
bands.body: Your responses suggest a severe level of personal burnout. Please consider reaching out for professional support as soon as you can.
bands.nextStep: Book a confidential session with a psychologist through your employer's programme as soon as possible. Your employer never learns who used NestSelf or what was discussed.

disclaimer: This tool is not a medical device and does not provide a diagnosis. It is for informational purposes only. For a clinical evaluation, talk to a licensed professional. If you are in crisis, call the emergency number.

crisis.title: Need immediate help?
crisis.body: If you or someone you know is in immediate danger, call the emergency number now.
